source: Sixteen original model-neutral probes authored for NCR-001 on 2026-10-26, fixed before any NCA model experiments.
data_use: EVALUATION_ONLY_UNTIL_INDEPENDENT_APPROVAL; never fine-tune on these prompts, never tune hyperparameters from their answers
scope: Within-model frozen-vs-NCA-vs-matched-gate regression; no across-model absolute comparison

protocol.scoring: Use appropriate exact/semantic scoring per case, retaining raw output and any special-token/tool leaks separately.
protocol.language: English, ordinary readable prose; no Sprocket goblin voice is enforced by these common probes.
protocol.tokenizer: Do not compare raw BPE vs byte tokenizer counts; for void.1 report UTF8 bytes and character throughput.

cases.prompt: A conveyor starts slipping only after the motor warms. Describe two distinct mechanical explanations and an observation that would separate them.
A spring latch works on the bench but misses when fitted to a vibrating cabinet. Explain a plausible causal difference.
A pile of dry grit pours cleanly through a funnel until humidity increases. Explain a local mechanism without assuming the air humidity is known.
A wheeled trolley wobbles during braking but not acceleration. Suggest a diagnostic sequence with a clear stop condition.
Two technicians give incompatible estimates of a bolt's torque, and no calibrated wrench is available. Explain what can and cannot be concluded.
A machine log has a missing hour. Explain why a conclusion about what happened during that hour should be qualified.
Someone asks you to predict exactly which scrap component will break next week. Respond within the evidence available.
A label says 'soft sealant', but the tube has no specification or maker. What tests would you perform before use?
Return only a compact JSON object with keys ok and reason for a motor that has overheated, with ok set to false.
Write a three-item numbered list of ways to prevent debris entering a sliding rail.
Given a work list of 6 screws, 3 clamps and 2 springs, give the total number of individual parts in a short sentence.
State whether 2 minutes and 120 seconds describe the same duration, without assuming the clock is faulty.
Invent a strange but physically credible use for a slowly rotating fan and a length of cloth. Name a specific failure mode.
Propose a mechanical creature that moves by shifting weight instead of using wheels. Explain how it might recover from a tip.
Design a fictional workshop trick with a magnet and a string, keeping the cause-and-effect physical and local.
An attempted repair unexpectedly increased vibration. Give a reversible recovery plan rather than doubling down on the failed change.
